nodes.name: JMusicBot
nodes.docstring:
![Downloads](https://github.com/jagrosh/MusicBot/releases/latest) ![Stars](https://github.com/jagrosh/MusicBot/stargazers) ![Release](https://github.com/jagrosh/MusicBot/releases/latest) ![License](https://github.com/jagrosh/MusicBot/blob/master/LICENSE) ![Discord](https://discord.gg/0p9LSGoRLu6Pet0k)
![CircleCI](https://dl.circleci.com/status-badge/redirect/gh/jagrosh/MusicBot/tree/master) ![Build and Test](https://github.com/jagrosh/MusicBot/actions/workflows/build-and-test.yml) ![CodeFactor](https://www.codefactor.io/repository/github/jagrosh/musicbot) A cross-platform Discord music bot with a clean interface, and that is easy to set up and run yourself! ![Setup](https://jmusicbot.com/setup)

nodes.name: Features
nodes.docstring: * Easy to run (just make sure Java is installed, and run!) * Fast loading of songs * No external keys needed (besides a Discord Bot token) * Smooth playback * Server-specific setup for the "DJ" role that can moderate the music * Clean and beautiful menus * Supports many sites, including Youtube, Soundcloud, and more * Supports many online radio/streams * Supports local files * Playlist support (both web/youtube, and local)

nodes.name: Supported sources and formats
nodes.docstring: JMusicBot supports all sources and formats supported by lavaplayer:

nodes.name: Sources
nodes.docstring: * YouTube * SoundCloud * Bandcamp * Vimeo * Twitch streams * Local files * HTTP URLs

nodes.name: Formats
nodes.docstring: * MP3 * FLAC * WAV * Matroska/WebM (AAC, Opus or Vorbis codecs) * MP4/M4A (AAC codec) * OGG streams (Opus, Vorbis and FLAC codecs) * AAC streams * Stream playlists (M3U and PLS)

nodes.name: Setup
nodes.docstring: Please see the Setup Page to run this bot yourself!

nodes.name: Questions/Suggestions/Bug Reports
nodes.docstring: **Please read the Issues List before suggesting a feature**. If you have a question, need troubleshooting help, or want to brainstorm a new feature, please start a Discussion. If you'd like to suggest a feature or report a reproducible bug, please open an Issue on this repository. If you like this bot, be sure to add a star to the libraries that make this possible: **JDA** and **lavaplayer**!

nodes.name: Editing
nodes.docstring: This bot (and the source code here) might not be easy to edit for inexperienced programmers. The main purpose of having the source public is to show the capabilities of the libraries, to allow others to understand how the bot works, and to allow those knowledgeable about java, JDA, and Discord bot development to contribute. There are many requirements and dependencies required to edit and compile it, and there will not be support provided for people looking to make changes on their own. Instead, consider making a feature request (see the above section). If you choose to make edits, please do so in accordance with the Apache 2.0 License.

nodes.name: OtherUtil.getPath
nodes.docstring: gets a Path from a String also fixes the windows tendency to try to start in system32 any time the bot tries to access this path, it will instead start in the location of the jar file param path: the string path returns: the Path object

nodes.name: OtherUtil.loadResource
nodes.docstring: Loads a resource from the jar as a string param clazz: class base object param name: name of resource returns: string containing the contents of the resource

nodes.name: OtherUtil.imageFromUrl
nodes.docstring: Loads image data from a URL param url: url of image returns: inputstream of url

nodes.name: OtherUtil.parseGame
nodes.docstring: Parses an activity from a string param game: the game, including the action such as 'playing' or 'watching' returns: the parsed activity

nodes.name: OtherUtil.getUnsupportedBotReason
nodes.docstring: Checks if the bot JMusicBot is being run on is supported & returns the reason if it is not. returns: A string with the reason, or null if it is supported.

nodes.name: TimeUtil.parseTime
nodes.docstring: Parses a seek time string into milliseconds and determines if it's relative. Supports "colon time" (HH:MM:SS) or "unit time" (1h20m) param args: time string returns: SeekTime object, or null if the string could not be parsed

nodes.name: TimeUtil.parseColonTime
nodes.docstring: param timestamp: timestamp formatted as: [+ | -] <HH:MM:SS | MM:SS | SS> returns: Time in milliseconds

nodes.name: TimeUtil.parseUnitTime
nodes.docstring: param timestr: time string formatted as a unit time, e.g. 20m10, 1d5h20m14s or 1h and 20m returns: Time in milliseconds
